issues.description: panLinear/zoomLinear now silently coerce null/undefined to 0 instead of preserving original toNumber behavior
issues.detail: Original code passed toNumber directly as lift; null/undefined entries became null and propagated as NaN through arithmetic. New coerceNumber maps null/undefined to 0, which changes output values for callers with null domain endpoints (e.g. ordinal-like domains). This is a behavioral regression not documented in 'same runtime behavior as before'.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the emptiness check, so empty input still calls Math.sign(undefined)=NaN
issues.detail: panLog and zoomLog compute `Math.sign(domain[0])` before invoking pan/zoom, so the error thrown by isNonEmpty never fires for these entry points on empty arrays. The user gets a NaN-poisoned result or an error from log(NaN), not the intended 'Domain array must not be empty'. Move the check to each exported function or to before sign computation.

issues.description: Domain return type [number, number] is too narrow given log/symlog can produce NaN
issues.detail: Functions are typed to return Domain = [number, number], but log(sign) applied to a non-matching-sign value or pow with negative base yield NaN. Consumers relying on this type will assume finite numbers. Either widen the type or document that NaN is possible — silently lying in types undermines the typesafe goal of the PR.

issues.description: Test coverage for the new error path only exercises panLinear and zoomLinear
issues.detail: The empty-domain error is added to pan() and zoom(), but tests only cover panLinear/zoomLinear. Given the panLog/zoomLog issue above, adding tests for Log/Pow/Symlog variants with empty domains would have caught the early Math.sign(domain[0]) bug.

issues.description: Introducing a runtime throw in a refactor PR is a behavior change worth a version note
issues.detail: The PR description acknowledges this is a new runtime error, but vega-util is a published library and prior callers passing [] would have received [NaN, NaN] silently. Worth a changeset/changelog entry and a minor (not patch) bump, otherwise downstream packages may break unexpectedly on upgrade.

issues.description: peek overload ordering is fine but the readonly tuple type loses information after destructuring
issues.detail: The new overload `peek<T>(array: readonly [T, ...T[]]): T` helps when domain is typed as NonEmptyArray, but pan/zoom pass `domain: number[]` after the isNonEmpty guard — TypeScript narrows in-scope, yet peek(domain) still resolves to the wider overload since `domain` parameter type isn't re-narrowed inside the call. Consider passing the narrowed reference or annotating the param as NonEmptyArray.

review.summary: The refactor cleanly migrates transform.js to TypeScript and adds a peek overload, but introduces two real concerns: panLog/zoomLog compute Math.sign(domain[0]) before the empty-domain guard fires, so empty inputs don't actually hit the new error, and coerceNumber silently maps null/undefined to 0 — a behavior change from the original toNumber-only lift. The new runtime throw also deserves a changelog/semver note since published callers passing [] previously got NaN values silently. Tests should cover the Log/Pow/Symlog empty-domain paths, not just Linear.
